title: Multimodal AI
description: How models that understand text, images, audio, and video work — and how to use them effectively.

data.text: Multimodal AI refers to models that can process and understand multiple types of input — text, images, audio, video — within the same architecture. Unlike earlier AI systems that handled one modality at a time, multimodal models learn shared representations that connect concepts across different sensory inputs. This enables use cases like describing an image, answering questions about a video, or generating images from text descriptions.

Most modern multimodal models use a 'shared embedding space' architecture. Each modality has its own encoder (e.g., a vision transformer for images, a text encoder for text, an audio encoder for sound). These encoders project their inputs into a common high-dimensional space where related concepts across modalities cluster together. A large language model then operates in this shared space, reasoning over and generating across modalities.

data.text: Text-to-image models like DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and Ideogram translate text descriptions into images using diffusion models. Diffusion works by starting with random noise and iteratively denoising it guided by the text prompt. The model learns to associate text concepts with visual patterns during training on billions of image-text pairs.

data.title: Major text-to-image models:
items: DALL-E 3 — integrated into ChatGPT and Bing; strong prompt following
Midjourney — artistic, aesthetic-focused; community-driven prompt culture
Stable Diffusion — open-source; runs locally; highly customizable
Ideogram — strong at text rendering in images; handles complex compositions
Flux — open-weight, high quality; fast inference with optimized samplers

data.text: Vision-language models take an image as input and respond with text — essentially 'seeing' and 'understanding' what's in the image. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini all have vision capabilities. You can upload a photo and ask 'What's in this image?' or 'Can you help me debug this code screenshot?' — and the model analyzes the pixels directly.

data.title: VLMs don't 'see' like humans
data.text: Vision-language models process images as grids of pixel values or patch embeddings. They don't have biological vision, depth perception, or real-world experience. They've learned statistical patterns between visual features and text descriptions during training — incredibly impressive, but fundamentally different from human perception.

Multimodal models increasingly handle audio. Speech-to-text models like OpenAI's Whisper transcribe speech with near-human accuracy. Text-to-speech models like ElevenLabs and OpenAI's TTS generate natural-sounding speech from text. The next generation of models processes all modalities together — understanding the tone of a speaker's voice while analyzing what they're saying.

data.title: Multimodal use cases
data.content:
1. Customer support: User sends a photo of a broken product + voice message describing the issue. The VLM analyzes both and generates a text response with troubleshooting steps.

2. Education: A student uploads a screenshot of a math problem. The VLM reads the problem, identifies the mathematical concept, and generates a step-by-step solution with a text explanation.

3. Content creation: A marketer uploads a product photo and writes a prompt for a social media caption. The VLM describes the image accurately and generates platform-appropriate copy.

4. Accessibility: A visually impaired user takes a photo of their surroundings. The VLM describes the scene in detail, reads any visible text, and answers follow-up questions.

data.text: Video understanding is the hardest multimodal frontier. A video is a sequence of images (frames) plus possibly audio. Models must process temporal relationships — what happened before, what's happening now, what's likely next. GPT-4o and Gemini can process video uploads, and specialized models like VideoLLaMA and TimeChat are built specifically for video understanding tasks.

For practical video AI today, upload short clips (under 2 minutes) to a VLM. For longer videos, extract key frames or transcripts and process them separately. Full video understanding is improving rapidly but still has significant limitations.

data.title: Current limitations:
items: Hallucination — VLMs can describe objects that aren't in the image
Spatial reasoning — difficulty with precise locations, distances, and counts
Text in images — struggling with distorted, stylized, or small text
Temporal understanding — videos are harder than images; causality is still weak
3D understanding — depth, perspective, and occlusion remain challenging
Cultural context — models trained on Western data may misinterpret global imagery

terms.definition: An AI system that can process multiple types of input (text, image, audio, video) in a unified architecture.
A model that combines computer vision and natural language understanding to analyze images and respond with text.
A generative model that creates images by iteratively denoising random noise, guided by a text prompt.

data.title: Summary
points: Multimodal models process text, images, audio, and video in shared architectures
VLMs enable image understanding through text descriptions
Text-to-image uses diffusion models guided by text prompts
Audio models handle transcription (Whisper) and generation (ElevenLabs)
Video understanding requires temporal reasoning over frame sequences
Current limitations include hallucination, spatial reasoning, and cultural context
data.takeaway: Multimodal AI is collapsing the boundaries between sensory modalities, enabling natural interaction with AI through whatever medium is most convenient.
